grades.reason: Notes on races, spinlocks, and Java/POSIX APIs. It says nothing about why condition-variable waits belong in a while loop.

grades.quote: For this reason sleep is always called inside a loop that re-checks the condition, as in P above.
grades.reason: This passage explains xv6's sleep/wakeup, which works like a condition-variable wait. It says why sleep is always called in a loop: a wakeup can be spurious, because several sleepers share a channel or channels collide, so each woken process must re-check the condition and sleep again.

The BoundedBuffer example puts wait() inside while loops, so it shows the idiom. The passage never explains why a loop is needed, such as spurious wakeups or conditions changing before the waiter runs.

grades.quote: wakeup(chan) wakes up all processes (if any) that have called sleep(chan, ...) with the same chan value.
grades.reason: The passage shows the check-condition-then-sleep pattern, with piperead calling sleep inside a while loop. It also notes that wakeup wakes all waiters on a channel. It never says why the wait is in a while loop instead of an if, such as rechecking after a wakeup, spurious wakeups, or another waiter consuming the condition. Its main concern is lost wake-ups and the condition lock, so it helps only a little.
